IGA: International general aviation (civil aviation operations other than scheduled air services and air transport)
IM: Inner marker (keying signal at 75 MHz marking the innermost ILS approach fix, typically at or near the runway threshold)
IMC: Instrument meteorological conditions (weather conditions requiring flight by reference to instruments rather than visual reference)
IMG: Immigration (government procedures for the entry and processing of persons at an international airport)
IMPR: Improve or improving (trend indicator used in meteorological and operational reports to indicate conditions are getting better)
IMT: Immediate or immediately (urgency qualifier in NOTAM text requiring prompt action)
INA: Initial approach (first segment of an instrument approach procedure from the initial approach fix to the intermediate fix)
INBD: Inbound (aircraft or track proceeding toward a navigation aid, waypoint, or aerodrome)
INC: In cloud (flight condition where the aircraft is operating within a cloud layer)
INCORP: Incorporated (indicates that an entity or organization is legally constituted as a corporation)
INFO: Information (factual data or operational details communicated in aviation messages and reports)
INOP: Inoperative (equipment, system, or facility that is not functioning or unavailable for use)
INP: If not possible (contingency qualifier in NOTAM text indicating alternative action when primary action cannot be performed)
INPR: In progress (activity or operation currently underway and not yet completed)
INS: Inertial navigation system (self-contained navigation system using accelerometers and gyroscopes to compute position without external references)
INSTR: Instrument (device or system used for measurement, control, or navigation; also refers to instrument flight procedures)
INT: Intersection (point where two or more airways, routes, or navigation fixes cross)
INTL: International (operations, flights, or facilities involving two or more countries)
INTRG: Interrogator (transmitter in a secondary surveillance radar system that sends interrogation signals to aircraft transponders)
INTSF: Intensify or intensifying (trend indicator used in weather reports to indicate increasing strength of a phenomenon)
INTST: Intensity (measure of the strength or magnitude of a meteorological phenomenon, such as precipitation or turbulence)
IR: Ice on runway (presence of frozen water on a runway surface, significantly affecting braking action)
IRS: Inertial reference system (electronic system providing aircraft attitude, heading, and position data using inertial sensors)
ISA: International standard atmosphere (standardized model of atmospheric pressure, temperature, and density used for aviation performance calculations)
ISB: Independent sideband (radio transmission technique where two separate sidebands carry independent information channels)
ISOL: Isolated (meteorological term describing weather phenomena occurring in separated or scattered locations)
JAN: January (first month of the year, used in dates in aviation documentation and NOTAM text)
JTST: Jet stream (narrow, high-altitude air current of strong winds, typically affecting flight planning and fuel efficiency)
JUL: July (seventh month of the year, used in dates in aviation documentation and NOTAM text)
JUN: June (sixth month of the year, used in dates in aviation documentation and NOTAM text)
KG: Kilograms (metric unit of mass used for aircraft weight, payload, and fuel measurements)
KHZ: Kilohertz (unit of frequency equal to 1000 hertz, used for radio navigation and communication frequencies)
KIAS: Knots indicated airspeed (airspeed reading from the pitot-static system, uncorrected for position and instrument errors)
KM: Kilometres (metric unit of distance equal to 1000 metres, used for visibility and distance reporting)
KMH: Kilometres per hour (metric unit of speed, used in some regions for wind speed and aircraft ground speed reporting)
KPA: Kilopascal (metric unit of pressure used for atmospheric pressure and tyre pressure measurements)
KT: Knots (unit of speed equal to one nautical mile per hour, standard for aviation speed measurements)
KW: Kilowatts (unit of power equal to 1000 watts, used for engine power ratings and electrical system specifications)
LAN: Inland (area away from coastlines, used in meteorological and navigational context)
LAT: Latitude (angular distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees, used for position fixing)
LDA: Landing distance available (length of runway declared available and suitable for the ground landing run of an aircraft)
LDG: Landing (phase of flight during which an aircraft descends to and touches down on a runway or landing surface)
LDI: Landing direction indicator (visual device indicating the direction of landing, such as a tetrahedron or wind indicator)
LEN: Length (measurement of the longest dimension of a runway, taxiway, or other facility)
LF: Low frequency (30 to 300 kHz) (radio frequency band used for long-range navigation aids such as NDBs and LORAN)
LGT: Light or lighting (illumination equipment or condition, used in reference to runway, approach, or obstruction lights)
LGTD: Lighted (equipped with illumination, typically referring to runways, taxiways, or obstacles that are lit)
LIH: Light intensity high (brightest setting of aeronautical ground lighting, used in high visibility conditions)
LIL: Light intensity low (dimmed setting of aeronautical ground lighting, used in low visibility or night conditions)
LIM: Light intensity medium (intermediate setting of aeronautical ground lighting between low and high)
